missing: SCOPE OF THIS CRITIQUE: I checked the design against the flow tree at main aab0d132 on 2026-11-11 and against gaps-full.md, sections G1-G8, G11-G13 and G16. I did not open the four report-*.md files (zazen, AI-DLC, lifecycle map, runtime map), so nothing below rests on them.

Verified: the gate's treatment of the goal's own verification commands is missing. flow-run-deterministic-checks.sh reports `trusted` and `not_executed` (lines 13-19), and settings.json:149 sets goals.executeVerificationCommands to false. The design never says whether `not_executed` or `incomplete_acs` fails the gate. The bigger problem is where the commands come from. The build worker writes them into the goal, and flow-goal-record.sh adds new goals to the per-user trust ledger automatically (flow-goal-record.sh:460-478; flow-goal-trust.sh keys on commands_sha256). So the gate, which runs outside every hook, executes commands the branch's own model chose. The `criterion_results` that 'replace the approver's spot-check' are therefore graded by the same model that wrote the code. G6 is satisfied for gate.commands but not for this half of the gate.

Verified: the other blocking asks in /flow:start have no plan. The spec stage removes only the specification-capture ask (start.md:254). These remain: zero acceptance criteria (219), a criterion that BLOCKS in the Spec Validation Gate (314), the Stranger Test (692), the permission to skip build-and-run (999), runtime verification (1008), and NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW or requireAllPass=false (1125). In `-p` each of these becomes a stored question, and a `Blocking: yes` question parks the job. The design needs a list of every [ask: decision|permission] in start, pr, review, address and resolve that can block in factory mode, an expected park rate, and for each one either an intake guarantee that prevents it or acceptance that the job parks.

Verified: goal creation is not guaranteed. start.md:474-476 skips the goal when goalCreation is `auto` (the default, settings.json:146) and no criterion has a verification command, and a project file can set `off`. The build→open_pr guard requires an achieved goal, so these jobs fail that guard on every attempt. The factory has to force goal creation or define a postcondition for jobs with no goal. A FLOW_USER_SETTINGS copy cannot force it, because project and local settings outrank the user tier (cascade-resolve.sh:5-9).

Verified: credentials for workers that push. KEEP_ENV_NAMES (flow-eval-run.sh:150-157) has no GH_TOKEN, GH_HOST, GH_CONFIG_DIR, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GIT_SSH_COMMAND or GPG/signing variables. The eval harness never pushes, but factory workers push and call gh, and running them under `env -i <KEEP_ENV>` loses token or SSH-agent auth on many setups. The design must say which auth variables are added. P5 should test a real push and a `gh pr create` from inside a worker.

Verified: the interactive executor has nothing to wake it. Judges, GitHub sync, needs-info replies, base moves, CI and human merges produce no background-task notification. After `wait` or `idle` ends the turn, nothing re-enters until the user types, so G1 (queue drain) is not met for this executor. It needs a wake source, such as /loop, Monitor or a cron prompt, or the judges must also run as background Bash calls.

Verified: G16 on the PR side. In the rework stage, /flow:address fetches every inline and conversation comment with no author filter (address.md:126 and 173). The ready→rework transition fires on 'a CHANGES_REQUESTED review' with no trust check, so on a public repository anyone can start a round and have their text read by a worker that holds tools. Trust filtering for PR comments, reviews and the PR body is not designed.

Verified: the issue title is not covered by G16. flow-issue-text.sh is described as quoting the body and the trusted comments only. The title is printed raw at start.md:171-173 (TITLE=), pr.md:118, commit.md:92 and convention-enforcement SKILL.md:44 reads the issue too. The inventory of raw issue reads covers start.md and branch-and-task-management only. It leaves out pr.md, commit.md, review.md:527 and convention-enforcement.

Verified: G3 is missing worktree bootstrap. A new worktree has no installed dependencies and no gitignored env files such as .env or local config. No stage installs dependencies, and there is no setting for a per-repo bootstrap command that runs from the base ref. Port isolation also leaves other shared resources open: database names, docker compose project names and build caches.

Verified: worker-side Tier 2 `confirm` is not handled. The design handles `confirm` only for writes the engine makes. Workers run `git push` and `gh pr create` from /flow:pr, and `gh pr review` and `gh pr comment` from review.md:2208 and 2303. When a user has set tiers.push or tiers.prCreate to confirm, tier-gate asks, and in `-p` an ask is a refusal (three-tier-safety.md:77). The open_pr and review stages then fail every attempt with no clear reason recorded. Either the engine performs those writes, or the pre-launch check reads the tier keys and parks the job in waiting_operator.

Verified: the transitions table has states with no exit and states with no entry. needs_spec_approval has no outgoing row. waiting_operator and waiting_ci are named in the text but appear in no row. needs_info has no row for when intake.maxRounds runs out. needs_human after state-tampered has no exit except `rebuild`, which is not a transition. Ready→approve (switch on) followed by approve→ready (interactive executor) repeats forever unless a guard records that an approval ask was already made at this head SHA.

Verified: G8 is not covered for ready jobs. Ready holds no slot, and the base can move while a person has not yet merged. No transition re-gates a ready job when the base moves; the only head-change rows cover the PR head. Either the engine watches ready jobs for base moves, or setup requires GitHub's 'require branches to be up to date' rule, which setup.md does not offer according to gaps-full.md G8.

Verified: rework (/flow:address) posts FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE markers itself (address.md:1352-1380). Under the design's rule that only the review worker's markers count, rework resolutions are discarded. The design must say how a round's ledger balances. The factory's ledger and the human /flow:merge ledger, which trusts by cascade author_association (merge.md:304-379), would also disagree about the same PR.

Verified: setup gaps. The design adds a /flow:factory command, but the project-CLAUDE.md commands table that /flow:setup writes, the README command list and the router help also need it. Version sync points are plugin.json and marketplace.json, which the design names, and grep confirms only those two hold 3.16.0. Count-bearing text in the README and marketplace.json descriptions should be grepped at release.

Inferred: approval for the live acceptance run. That run creates issues, comments and PRs on a sandbox GitHub repository. Under the repository's hard boundary on external communication it needs the user's explicit approval, which the plan does not mention.

Inferred: the security surface is not routed under G11. G11 names 'security adds a stronger security reviewer'. The design keeps security-reviewer always on but does not raise its model when intake reports the security surface.
wrong: Verified: the goal binding to the head commit cannot survive a rework. flow-goal-record.sh:287-294 gives achieved no outgoing transition, and lines 446-452 say an achieved goal never changes. `lifecycle.last_evaluation.head_sha`, written at start.md step 9a, therefore stays at the build commit. After any review fix-forward, rework round or base-sync merge, 'goal achieved with head_sha == H' can never hold, and rewriting the field would trip goal_freeze. Phase-2 eligibility fails for every PR that had a second round. The proposed /flow:merge 'blocks on a mismatch' would also break ordinary non-factory PRs that got a fix-forward after start. The binding needs a re-evaluation record per SHA, kept apart from the lifecycle that cannot change, not one field in the lifecycle.

Verified: build is not idempotent once the goal is terminal. start.md:482 meets a terminal goal (achieved, failed or cancelled) with a blocking [ask: permission], so a build retry after the goal reached achieved, or a rework that re-enters start, parks the job. The G13 claim that '/flow:start continues an existing goal' holds only for goals that are not terminal (start.md:481).

Verified: marker provenance checks the wrong place. FLOW_REVIEW_CYCLE is posted as a PR review body through `gh pr review` (review.md:2208; merge.md:168 and 373-379 read pulls/N/reviews). Only FLOW_RESOLUTION_CYCLE is an issue comment (review.md:2303). A snapshot of 'the PR's comment ids' never sees the review markers, so the trusted ledger is always empty or incomplete.

Verified: the pre-launch protected check misses files the worker creates locally. The check compares origin/<base> with HEAD. A worker can create the untracked or gitignored files `.claude/settings.local.json` (loaded by `--setting-sources project,local`) and `.claude/settings.flow.local.json` (read first by cascade-resolve.sh:8 and 34-37) in the worktree. A commit diff does not see them, and the 'clean tree' guard ignores gitignored files. The next worker then loads hooks or settings the previous worker planted. The check must also refuse any untracked or ignored file under protected paths, using `git status --ignored` or by deleting them before launch.

Verified: the per-worker FLOW_USER_SETTINGS copy cannot steer workers. Project and local settings outrank the user tier (cascade-resolve.sh:5-9). `autonomous:true` in the copy loses to a project `autonomous:false` (flow-ask-policy.sh:32-34), and the same holds for goalCreation, tddMode, closedLoop, visualVerification, reviewCycleLimit and similar keys. Any setting the factory needs fixed has to be enforced by FACTORY_CONTEXT logic inside the commands, not by the user tier.

Verified: the security model states the wrong reason for the engine applying Tier 2 keys itself. The design says the engine does so 'because hooks do not see a script's own calls'. Under the interactive executor, however, the engine runs from session Bash with flow's git and gh wrappers first on PATH (three-tier-safety.md:80-86, hooks/shims/git and hooks/shims/gh). The wrappers do see the engine's push and comment calls: journal writes a second breadcrumb, and confirm exits 1 because tier-gate asked nothing. Headless, the wrappers are absent. One engine therefore behaves differently under the two executors, and the E2E claim of an 'identical final job.json' will not hold under confirm.

Verified: the read-guard hook cannot cover flow's own issue reads. start.md (line 151), pr.md, review.md and address.md fetch the issue in ```! blocks, which run when the command expands and not through the Bash tool, so PreToolUse hooks never see them. The guard only catches calls the model makes later. Every ```! block that reads the issue has to change; the hook adds nothing for those.

Verified: the tamper hash is not a protection against a worker. `.job.sha256` is unkeyed and sits next to job.json, and workers run as the same OS user with Bash. A worker can rewrite both files. The design lists 'A worker writes job.json' as a prevented failure mode, which overstates it: the hash detects accidental writes only.

Verified: two items are labelled unverified but are already answered or work differently. Per-dispatch Agent `model` (probe P2) is already relied on at review.md:1065-1087 (Path A: 'dispatch override > frontmatter > session model'), so only its use under `-p` is unknown. The dependency category, defined as 'any DEP_* line from flow-dep-diff.sh', also fires on DEP_BASELINE and DEP_REMOVED (flow-dep-diff.sh:32-37). Any change to a manifest then escalates, so the category should name DEP_ADDED, DEP_CHANGED, DEP_INSTALL_HOOK and DEP_REPLACED.

Verified: the portability assumptions fail on macOS, which is this machine. `/bin/bash` is 3.2.57, which has no `wait -n` (the headless runner's wait primitive). The `setsid` and `flock` command-line tools are absent (`which` finds neither), and only gtimeout and timeout come from Homebrew. The runner must use Python (os.setsid, fcntl) or require a newer bash, as flow-judge.sh already handles timeout versus gtimeout.

Inferred: the user-only switch check can miss an in-repo plugin copy. When cwd is an external worktree, cascade-resolve judges 'inside the repository' against that worktree's git top, not the main checkout. A plugin copy in the main checkout (dogfooding from this marketplace repository) is then not 'inside', so the claim that 'the in-repo install refusal keeps it off' fails unless user-only reads always run from the main checkout and also check against it.

Inferred: process-group handling can run two workers in one worktree. If the launcher is killed (for example when the interactive session ends) while claude runs under setsid in its own session, claude keeps running as an orphan. A liveness check on the launcher pid then reports the worker dead, and the stale-lease relaunch starts a second worker in the same worktree. The lease must record the claude process-group id and kill it, or confirm it is gone, before reissuing the stage.
unverified_assumptions: The spec bypass depends on the staleness rule in specification-journal-format.md:111, which compares the issue's `updatedAt` with the git commit date of the journal file. Several things move updatedAt after the spec commit: the engine's own labels and comments (flow:in-progress, question comments), /flow:start's `gh issue edit --add-assignee`, and every retry. The spec may then be treated as stale and its elements drafted and asked again, which brings back the blocking ask. Spike: run /flow:start under `-p` after a label change that follows the spec commit.

That ```! command blocks run in `claude -p "/flow:start N"` with `--permission-prompts none` and a narrow `--allowedTools` list, and that their output reaches the model. P1 tests SessionStart and the wrappers but not the ```! blocks, which are the main way every flow command gathers context.

Workers load plugins and hooks that the project enables. `--setting-sources project,local` reads enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces from the worktree's .claude/settings.json. For example, this repository's settings enable typesafe@typesafe-ai. A second flow copy enabled at project level would register duplicate hooks and colliding command names next to `--plugin-dir`. This needs a spike.

How flow's Stop hook (flow-goal-stop.sh, with project-set stopHookEnforcement block or evaluator-loop) and its SessionEnd hooks (session-end-learn.sh, session-end-state.sh) behave in `-p` workers for the pr, review and address stages while the issue's goal is active and not achieved. They may hold the worker open until --max-turns, or write learn proposals for every worker. This needs a spike.
That `claude -p` with `--resume <session_id>` honours a new `--max-budget-usd` and `--max-turns`, and that cost reported after a resume is additive (P3 covers resume only).

That GitHub lets the factory's gh identity post a `gh pr review --comment` on its own PR in every repository configuration, and that review bodies posted that way carry the author_association the ledger expects. Probe P6 does not include this.

That `gh pr ready` and labels on a PR marked needs_human do not trigger CI or merge queues that a person did not intend. needs_human marks the PR ready, which on some repositories starts required workflows or notifies CODEOWNERS.

That the goal trust ledger in the shared per-user FLOW_STATE_DIR (goal-trust.jsonl) is safe under concurrent appends from several workers, and that its entries do not trust goals across worktrees by mistake. The design names this risk but sets no probe. flow-eval-run.sh avoids it by giving each run its own FLOW_STATE_DIR (line 870), and the design does not.

That the intake judge's fact sheet (ls-tree plus the first 200 lines of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md) is enough to grade risk and surfaces, and that the effective risk 'max(intake, deterministic)' is not lowered by the branch. flow-risk-check.sh reads design.riskAreas through the full cascade, including the worktree's project and local files (flow-risk-check.sh:18-25), unless factory mode reads it with --repo-settings-ref.
